correctness.rationale: The fixed-point semantics permit replacing witnesses by inclusion-minimal neighborhoods. If every horizontal minimum is a singleton, a single row suffices; if the vertical minimum is unique, it lies in every witnessing row and supplies the common vertical set. If both alternatives fail, restrict nonempty rows to one horizontal minimum of size at least two and put distinct vertical minima in two of its rows. A rectangle witness is forced to use that entire horizontal minimum, and the intersection of those rows contains no vertical neighborhood. This proves necessity with the right nonemptiness hypotheses. Interchanging coordinates gives the other criterion. On t labelled points there are T_t permitted antichains, S_t in each of the two favorable classes and t in their overlap. This gives E by inclusion–exclusion and J by the four disjoint left classes, with right counts T_n,S_n,S_n,n. At every pair the local disjunction is equivalent to all left worlds satisfying the first condition or all right worlds the second, proving the global count and rarity by the middle-layer bound for D_t. At a point-containing right carrier of size ≤2 the allowed sets form a chain, and on a left singleton carrier all minima are singletons; the explicit 2×3 valuation therefore witnesses the first possible failure in that orientation. The finite checker was read, not executed; it is not needed for the universal proof.
